title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI system was used to generate non-consensual sexual images of a real person without her knowledge or permission. The person who deployed the system obtained source photographs from the victim's social media account, then distributed the generated images across multiple platforms using anonymous accounts to conceal his identity. The deployment happened outside any legitimate use case, driven by personal animosity toward the target.

This is a case of impersonation and image-based abuse enabled by generative AI. Detection would have required either the victim or platform moderators to identify the fake content and report it, which did occur, or for the person to have been stopped before distributing the material. It is not established what technical safeguards, if any, the AI system itself had to prevent non-consensual intimate image generation.

The investigation traced the perpetrator through digital forensics and his own admissions. It is not established whether the AI tool used had terms of service prohibiting this use, or what role platform design played in enabling the distribution.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create fake explicit images and videos. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook, while using several Gmail addresses to hide his identity. The woman reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station after receiving messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her morphed images were being shared on Discord servers.

Police launched an investigation and analyzed digital footprints, email accounts, and technical evidence to trace the fake profiles back to Bansal. During questioning, Bansal admitted he knew the woman from college and had developed a personal grudge against her following repeated conflicts. He also revealed that other unknown users created additional explicit content using his initial uploads, which he then reshared. Authorities recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, and the investigation is continuing.
